content:
nora: hey all, day 1 here. trying to build runtime from source in our ubuntu20 dev container and hit a weird runtime loader error after linking. build finishes but running binary fails: 

nora: error when running ./bin/redwood-runtime:
```
./bin/redwood-runtime: error while loading shared libraries: libcublasLt.so.12: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

nora: `ls /usr/local/cuda/lib64` shows libcublasLt.so.12 present in /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64 but container has /usr/local/cuda -> /usr/local/cuda-11.8. I tried updating symlink but CI images expect /usr/local/cuda to be stable. any recommended approach?

tariq: welcome @nora! two approaches: 1) set RUNPATH at link time so binary looks in the right lib dir: add `-Wl,-rpath,/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64` to CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS OR 2) set LD_LIBRARY_PATH in the runtime wrapper script (we have scripts/runtime-launch.sh) to prefer the toolkit you built against. Both are fine for local dev; prefer rpath for reproducible binary.

nora: thanks. I grepped CMakeLists and found explicit `-lcublasLt_static` linked. switching to shared `cublasLt` plus adding rpath fixed the run. pushed branch `nora/rpath-cublas-fix` and CI runs.

build-bot: CI note: avoid embedding absolute vendor paths in release artifacts. For dev branches it's okay. On release we prefer dynamic resolution via packaging.

ops-bot: if you changed symlinks on a managed host, please file INFRA-6789. For ephemeral dev containers prefer using our image tags `redwood/dev-runtime:cuda-12.1` which match CI.

hannah: little tip: if you ever see different toolkit headers vs libs, `strings /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcublasLt.so | grep CUBLASLT` or `readelf -a` can show which toolkit built the library. welcome aboard and nice quick fix! :tada:

nora: thanks all 1 will tidy commit and request review. happy to pair if anyone wants to walk through setting rpath in the CMake macro.
